A.trend: No series; honestly stated as not measured.
A.chart: The only chart is an RR bar chart from memory, tagged to references and not labelled estimate.
A.dimensions: Only the evidence-magnitude chart, which comes from memory.
A.drilldown: Generic follow-ups given in words only.
A.refs: Both DOIs resolve but there are no quotes, and the 1.13 estimate is misattributed to Greenwood 2014.
A.accuracy: Imamura's adiposity-adjusted 1.13 (1.06-1.21) is attributed to Greenwood; Greenwood reported about 1.20 per 330 ml.
A.limits: Honest and specific about what was not measured.
A.integrity: Single chart renders with no console errors.
A.verdict: All four fields present, but the verdict contains no numbers and names no contrary evidence beyond observational design.
A.article: Under 2,000 words; an honest knowledge-only piece.

B.trend: Both lanes traced with window; May 2026 withheld as incomplete; growth and peak quantified. 'News faster from 2021' is slightly off: the 2021 index has research ahead.
B.comparison: Studied-vs-reported ratio for India and comparators, with the window mismatch stated; lift not used.
B.chart: Script ceiling 0: a counted chart (e.g. the RR chart, sourced only to ref:r1 but showing r2/r3 values) fails tracing.
B.dimensions: Time, geography, comparison, composition, forecast and source mix traced.
B.map: Two lanes mapped, patent lane stated empty, placed_pct carried, mismatch concluded. The England journal row is folded into GBR without comment.
B.forecast: Central and bounds traced; MAE vs no-change, baseline, gap to today and quantity all stated; bounds read as sensitivity, not probability.
B.drilldown: Themes, countries and documents carry identifiers; 7/7 follow-ups executable, none folded back.
B.export: Script ceiling 0: some rows do not trace (e.g. extra country rows or document rows).
B.repro: 367/371 numbers traced; calls declared with args.
B.refs: DOIs resolve and quotes are verbatim; the news items have URLs and dates.
B.accuracy: Says 5 of 7 read documents were unrelated; the tool tally says 13 unrelated with 2 supporting. The 18-month patent lag is untagged.
B.limits: Limits sit beside their numbers: end dates, censoring, placed_pct, top-N truncation, patent lag, and what would close each gap. It also catches the overcount where news rows exceed the placed total.
B.verdict: Four fields, traced numbers, thin intersection literature named as the contrary item.
B.crossdomain: Four corpora connected, lanes kept apart, and the mismatch quantified; the mismatch drives the funding recommendation.
B.article: Complete, traced and honest, with the counter-tally reported; the unrelated-count error appears in Results.

C.trend: Research series is full, but the news chart plots only selected landmark months as a line; growth, peak and censoring are stated.
C.comparison: No ratio between lanes. India is read only through an empty top-row result in a five-article news lane.
C.chart: Script ceiling 1: the news landmarks chart is not a full series.
C.dimensions: Time, evidence, composition, geography and forecast; the chart integrity issues reduce this.
C.map: One lane mapped with India present; the window is vague and placed_pct is absent because news.geography was not run.
C.forecast: Method, baseline, MAE, observed-through date, gap and quantity all stated; bounds read as sensitivity.
C.drilldown: No traced breakdown layer; follow-ups not verified.
C.export: Provenance present, but the news export is landmarks only and the patent row is malformed.
C.repro: All numbers traced, though some calls merge two features under one ID.
C.refs: Two references, both resolving, with verbatim quotes.
C.accuracy: Faithful reading of the tool output; correctly notes the factor tally is unavailable.
C.limits: Specific on end dates and lanes, but placed_pct and the lift baseline are missing.
C.crossdomain: Research, health and news connected; patent lane reported empty. The mismatch is not quantified.
C.article: Complete and traced, but the Discussion cites only two references.

D.comparison: Memory RRs contrasted across different exposure contrasts.
D.chart: Memory RR chart; methods admit the values were recalled.
D.drilldown: Key documents carry DOIs; follow-ups in words, none executed.
D.export: Mostly empty structure tables; key-document values from memory.
D.repro: Script ceiling 0: untagged and memory numbers.
D.accuracy: Recalled figures (Schulze 1.83, Malik 1.26, Imamura 1.18/1.13, Colchero 6%) match the literature.
D.limits: Honest and specific about the gaps and source age.
D.verdict: Low confidence and contrary items named, but the numbers come from memory.
D.article: Honest literature review with resolving DOIs; capped as a plain setup.

A: Greenwood 2014 given as RR 1.13 (1.06-1.21); that is Imamura 2015's adiposity-adjusted figure, and Greenwood reported about 1.20 per 330 ml/day
B: States 5 of 7 read documents were unrelated; tool tally c6 shows 2 supports and 13 unrelated
Chart ch_rr sourced only to ref:r1 but plots r2/r3 values
C: News chart draws a line through selected landmark months, not the full monthly series
News-about lane taken from a 5-article research.geography sample rather than the news geography call, so India's absence is weakly grounded
D: Effect sizes recalled from memory and tagged only to references; some numbers untagged

raw.verdict: B was the only deliverable to trace all four corpora, both attention lanes with censoring, two geography maps and a properly caveated forecast into one argument about the gap between where the topic is studied and where it is reported. Its weak points are an export and chart tracing failure and a misread of the unrelated-document count. C was traced but thinner and partial on the news and geography lanes; A and D were honest memory-only reviews, and A also misattributed a pooled estimate.
